newsitem.title: UK: Clean tanker rates steady to weaker in dull market.
newsitem.headline: Clean tanker rates steady to weaker in dull market.

text.p: Middle East clean tanker rates ended the week lower as refinery turnarounds and industry functions in London cut fixing activity, brokers said on Friday.
Rates for 30,000 tonne vessels headed out of the Middle East for India were quoted at of W220, while the 70,000 tonne Fly Eagle was reported fixed by Idemitsu at a rate of W165 loading March 22.
"Whilst it has been a disappointing week, the anticipated deliveries to India for March should result in these market levels improving," ship brokers Gibson said in their weekly report.
Rates for 55,000 tonners on long-haul trips out of the Middle East were also in the doldrums at around W205.
Mediterranean rates were also slightly easier after a generally quiet week.
"The clean products market in the Mediterranean struggled to maintain last week's levels with barely sufficient enquiry to employ available tonnage," the Gibson report said.

Rates for 27,500 tonners carrying naphtha on cross-Med trips were quoted at W270 against W280 last week, while 28-29,000 tonne vessels carrying gas oil on a similar route commanded around W215-225 against W240-250 seen last week.

The UK/Cont market remained steady with 20,000 tonne vessels doing UK/Cont trips commanding W230 the same as last week, while 25,000-tonne vessels coming into the sector from the Baltic Sea came in at W210.
Rates in the Caribbean were little changed with a 30,000 tonner going up U.S. coast put at $280 the same as last week.
